tools.name: Apache Arrow / PyArrow
tools.what_it_is: Language-agnostic columnar in-memory framework. Zero-copy data interchange between subsystems. PyArrow is the Python binding.
tools.what_it_is_not: A database. Not a query engine. Not a storage format (that's Parquet). Not a replacement for DuckDB or Postgres.
tools.maturity: Production-grade. Apache top-level project. PyArrow 19.x stable. Used by pandas 2.x, Polars, DuckDB, and many analytical tools.
tools.python_macos_compat: Pre-built wheels for macOS arm64 and x86_64, Linux, Windows. ~50MB wheel.
tools.transitive_dependency_risk: Low. PyArrow is a well-maintained library with infrequent breaking changes. DuckDB already interoperates with Arrow via the Apache Arrow C Data Interface.
tools.operational_complexity: Low for in-memory usage. Higher if using Arrow Flight or IPC files.
tools.duplicates_existing: No — no existing Arrow/columnar in-memory interchange in the codebase. DuckDB uses its own internal columnar format.
tools.risks_undermining_artifact_first: Low — Arrow is an in-memory format. Artifacts remain JSON/JSONL/CSV on disk. Arrow is a transient representation.
tools.risks_undermining_postgres_authority: None — Arrow is not a database. Postgres remains the operational substrate.
tools.helps_cockpit_ux: Yes — Arrow batches can reduce dict-of-dicts overhead in cockpit projection payloads.
tools.helps_static_docs: Low — batch offline renderer does not benefit from columnar in-memory format.
tools.helps_procurement: Moderate — procurement evidence packs assembled from multiple sources benefit from columnar batch processing.
tools.helps_github_integration: Low — GitHub packets are small JSON artifacts, not bulk data.
tools.helps_context_assembler: No — context assembly is CPU-bound tree-sitter parsing, not data interchange.
tools.helps_telemetry_evidence: Yes — Arrow tables can feed telemetry aggregate computation efficiently.
tools.recommendation: prototype — Phase 3. Prototype behind ProjectionStorePort as in-memory interchange for cockpit projections. Do not add until Postgres ports exist and projection comparison tests pass.

tools.name: Apache Parquet (via DuckDB)
tools.what_it_is: Column-oriented on-disk storage format with compression, encoding, and predicate pushdown. Already used via DuckDB COPY FORMAT PARQUET in compaction scripts.
tools.what_it_is_not: A canonical source-of-truth format. Not a database. Not a replacement for JSONL artifacts.
tools.maturity: Production-grade. Parquet is the dominant analytical snapshot format.
tools.license: Apache 2.0 (format is open; implementation via DuckDB which is MIT)
tools.python_macos_compat: No additional dependency — DuckDB already handles Parquet. PyArrow not required for Parquet read/write via DuckDB.
tools.transitive_dependency_risk: Zero — Parquet support is inside DuckDB, which is already a canonical dependency.
tools.operational_complexity: Low — existing compaction scripts already use this pattern.
tools.duplicates_existing: Already in use via DuckDB. No duplication.
tools.risks_undermining_artifact_first: Medium — Parquet snapshots MUST NOT become canonical event truth. They are derived analytical snapshots. JSON/JSONL remain source-of-truth. This doctrine must be enforced in tests.
tools.risks_undermining_postgres_authority: None — Parquet is cold/warm analytical storage. Postgres is the operational substrate.
tools.helps_cockpit_ux: Yes — Parquet snapshots seed cold-start without full JSONL reparse.
tools.helps_procurement: Yes — procurement evidence pack rollups as compressed Parquet derived snapshots.
tools.helps_github_integration: Moderate — GitHub alert lifecycle history and rate limit snapshots as Parquet rollups.
tools.helps_telemetry_evidence: Yes — telemetry aggregates and release-gate history as Parquet rollups.
tools.recommendation: promote — already in use. Formalize as the canonical derived analytical snapshot format. Add Parquet-snapshot-never-canonical contract test.

tools.name: ADBC / Arrow Flight
tools.what_it_is: ADBC (Arrow Database Connectivity) provides a standard API for Arrow-native database access. Arrow Flight is a high-performance gRPC-based transport for Arrow data.
tools.what_it_is_not: A database driver. Not a query engine. Flight is a network transport, not a local API.
tools.maturity: ADBC: early-adopter. Flight: production-grade for large-scale data transport.
tools.python_macos_compat: ADBC drivers for Postgres exist but are less mature than psycopg 3. Flight requires gRPC infrastructure.
tools.transitive_dependency_risk: High — ADBC/ Flight add gRPC, protobuf, and multiple C++ libraries. Substantial dependency surface.
tools.operational_complexity: High — Flight requires running Arrow Flight server. ADBC requires separate driver installation per database.
tools.duplicates_existing: psycopg 3 already provides efficient Postgres connectivity. DuckDB already provides efficient local analytics.
tools.helps_cockpit_ux: Low — local cockpit does not need high-throughput columnar transport.
tools.helps_telemetry_evidence: Low — local telemetry volumes are small. Flight is overkill.
tools.recommendation: park — audit later if hosted/team mode requires high-throughput Postgres→Arrow transport. Premature before Postgres ports and migrations exist.

tools.name: Polars
tools.what_it_is: Rust-backed DataFrame/query engine using Arrow columnar memory. Supports lazy evaluation, streaming, and expression-based transforms.
tools.what_it_is_not: A database. Not a replacement for DuckDB's SQL engine. Not a storage layer.
tools.python_macos_compat: Pre-built wheels for macOS arm64 and x86_64. ~25MB wheel. No system dependencies.
tools.transitive_dependency_risk: Low — well-maintained. But adds a second analytical engine alongside DuckDB, creating potential for divergent results.
tools.operational_complexity: Medium — requires learning Polars expression API alongside existing DuckDB SQL. Two analytical engines to maintain.
tools.duplicates_existing: Yes — DuckDB already provides 95% of Polars' analytical capability. DuckDB handles JSONL ingestion, Parquet compaction, and SQL-based aggregation natively.
tools.helps_cockpit_ux: Low — DuckDB already generates cockpit widget data.
tools.helps_static_docs: Low — static docs use Jinja2 templates, not DataFrame transforms.
tools.helps_procurement: Moderate — Polars lazy frames could streamline evidence pack generation from multiple JSONL sources with complex grouping. But DuckDB SQL can do the same.
tools.helps_github_integration: Low — GitHub packets are small artifacts.
tools.recommendation: park — DuckDB already dominates the analytical need. Add Polars only if measured projection/aggregation bottlenecks cannot be solved by DuckDB SQL. Evaluate after Phase 4 equivalence tests.

tools.name: Ibis
tools.what_it_is: Python-native expression layer that compiles to multiple SQL backends (DuckDB, Postgres, etc.). One expression, many backends.
tools.what_it_is_not: A query engine. Not a database. Ibis compiles expressions, not raw SQL.
tools.maturity: Production-grade. 8.x stable. Used by several enterprises for cross-backend analytics.
tools.python_macos_compat: Wheels available. Adds backend-specific dependencies (ibis-framework[duckdb], ibis-framework[postgres]).
tools.transitive_dependency_risk: Medium — Ibis 8.x has a growing dependency tree. Each backend adds its own dependencies.
tools.operational_complexity: Medium — Ibis adds an abstraction layer that must be tested against both DuckDB and Postgres backends. Expression debugging is harder than raw SQL.
tools.duplicates_existing: Partially — DuckDB SQL and future Postgres SQL cover the need. Ibis adds an abstraction over both.
tools.risks_undermining_postgres_authority: None — Ibis can target Postgres as a backend.
tools.helps_cockpit_ux: Low — cockpit widgets use simple SQL aggregations that don't need cross-backend portability.
tools.recommendation: park — raw SQL with contract tests is clearer and more auditable for Rig Relay's scale. Ibis adds abstraction overhead without clear benefit given the small number of backends (DuckDB + Postgres = 2). Re-evaluate if the number of analytical backends grows beyond 2.

tools.name: Apache DataFusion
tools.what_it_is: Rust-native Arrow-based SQL query engine. Embedded analytical engine, similar role to DuckDB but Arrow-native and Rust.
tools.what_it_is_not: A database with storage management. Not a replacement for DuckDB's broad format support (JSON, CSV, Parquet, Excel, etc.).
tools.maturity: Production-grade. Apache top-level project. Used by InfluxDB 3.0 and many other projects.
tools.python_macos_compat: Python bindings via datafusion-python. Less mature Python experience than DuckDB. Wheels available but less battle-tested.
tools.transitive_dependency_risk: Medium — datafusion-python is young relative to DuckDB. Smaller community.
tools.operational_complexity: High — Rust-native with Python FFI. Debugging and error messages are Rust-centric.
tools.duplicates_existing: Yes — DuckDB already provides an embedded analytical SQL engine with broader format support.
tools.helps_cockpit_ux: No — DuckDB already serves cockpit analytics.
tools.helps_other_domains: No clear advantage over DuckDB for any Rig Relay domain.
tools.recommendation: park — DuckDB dominates this need. DataFusion's Arrow-native architecture is interesting but adds complexity without measurable benefit. Revisit only if DuckDB proves insufficient for a specific Arrow-native workload.

tools.name: psycopg 3 COPY / binary COPY
tools.what_it_is: PostgreSQL's high-performance bulk data protocol. psycopg 3 supports both text COPY and binary COPY for maximum throughput.
tools.what_it_is_not: A replacement for schema validation. Not a query engine. Not a transport that bypasses constraints.
tools.maturity: Production-grade. PostgreSQL COPY is battle-tested for decades. psycopg 3 COPY implementation is stable.
tools.python_macos_compat: Full support via psycopg[binary]>=3.2. Pre-built wheels.
tools.transitive_dependency_risk: Low — psycopg 3 is the strategic Postgres driver. COPY is built-in.
tools.operational_complexity: Low to moderate. COPY FROM/TO with staging tables and constraint validation requires careful pipeline design.
tools.risks_undermining_artifact_first: Medium — COPY must NEVER bypass content-light enforcement, schema validation, or CHECK constraints. Use staging tables: COPY to staging → validate → promote. Never COPY directly to operational tables.
tools.risks_undermining_postgres_authority: None — COPY is native Postgres. Strengthens operational authority.
tools.helps_cockpit_ux: Yes — faster event_log ingestion means fresher cockpit data.
tools.helps_procurement: Yes — fast evidence backfills and export dumps for procurement packs.
tools.helps_github_integration: Yes — bulk GitHub event ingestion batches.
tools.helps_telemetry_evidence: Yes — bulk telemetry rollup ingestion and export.
tools.recommendation: promote — Phase 3 (Postgres Adapters). COPY is the most doctrine-aligned high-throughput Postgres ingestion/export pattern. Staging table + constraint promotion doctrine must be enforced in tests.

tools.name: pgvector
tools.what_it_is: PostgreSQL extension for vector similarity search. Stores embeddings as vector columns. Supports IVFFlat and HNSW indexing. Keeps vector search inside Postgres.
tools.what_it_is_not: A separate vector database. Not a general-purpose search engine. Not a replacement for full-text search or GIN indexes on JSONB.
tools.maturity: Production-grade. PG 0.8.x. Used by many enterprises. IVFFlat and HNSW indexes are stable.
tools.python_macos_compat: Postgres extension — must be installed in Postgres. pgvector Python client is lightweight. pip install pgvector.
tools.transitive_dependency_risk: Low — pgvector Python client is minimal. The extension itself is a Postgres compile-time extension.
tools.operational_complexity: Moderate — embeddings must be generated (requires an embedding model), stored as vector columns, and indexed. Embeddings over private repo content are sensitive derived data.
tools.duplicates_existing: No existing vector/semantic retrieval in Rig Relay.
tools.risks_undermining_artifact_first: Low — embeddings are derived data. Canonical artifacts remain JSON/JSONL/CSV.
tools.risks_undermining_postgres_authority: None — pgvector lives inside Postgres. Strengthens Postgres as the unified operational substrate.
tools.helps_cockpit_ux: Moderate — semantic search over content-light reports in admin dashboard.
tools.helps_github_integration: Moderate — similar GitHub alert lookup and remediation plan retrieval.
tools.helps_context_assembler: Yes — similar-failure and similar-remediation-plan retrieval from content-light report corpus.
tools.helps_telemetry_evidence: Moderate — semantic clustering of telemetry events.
tools.recommendation: park — Phase 6. Valuable but requires: (1) Postgres operational substrate to exist (Phase 3), (2) an approved sensitive-derived-data policy for embeddings, (3) an embedding model selection (local-only for private repo content). Embeddings over private repo content must be local-only and policy-approved. Audit as a separate slice.

tools.name: pg_jsonschema
tools.what_it_is: PostgreSQL extension that validates JSONB documents against JSON Schema directly in the database via CHECK constraints.
tools.what_it_is_not: A replacement for application-level jsonschema validation. Not a schema registry. Not a migration tool.
tools.maturity: Stable but niche. Fewer production deployments than pgvector. The extension must be compiled and installed in Postgres.
tools.python_macos_compat: Postgres extension — compile-time dependency. Not available via brew postgresql by default.
tools.transitive_dependency_risk: Low — single-purpose extension. No Python dependency.
tools.operational_complexity: Moderate — requires installing the extension in Postgres. Schema files must be synced between docs/schemas/ and the database. Schema versioning and updates are an operational concern.
tools.duplicates_existing: No — but jsonschema (Python) already validates at the application boundary. pg_jsonschema is defense-in-depth at the database boundary.
tools.risks_undermining_artifact_first: Low — complements file-based schema validation. Does not replace it.
tools.risks_undermining_postgres_authority: None — strengthens Postgres as a schema-enforcing operational substrate.
tools.helps_procurement: Yes — database-level schema enforcement is procurement-grade evidence that JSONB payloads are structurally valid.
tools.helps_telemetry_evidence: Yes — ensures event payloads and receipt envelopes are structurally valid at the database boundary.
tools.recommendation: park — Phase 5. Valuable defense-in-depth but requires: (1) Postgres operational substrate to exist (Phase 3), (2) schema registry to be populated (Phase 1), (3) pg_jsonschema extension availability in target Postgres environments. Application-level jsonschema validation remains the primary boundary — pg_jsonschema is strictly complementary.

tools.name: pgmq / Postgres-backed queues
tools.what_it_is: PostgreSQL-backed message queue. pgmq uses a table with polling/NOTIFY for queue semantics. Alternative: SKIP LOCKED pattern on a queue table.
tools.what_it_is_not: A high-throughput message broker like RabbitMQ or Kafka. Not suitable for >10k msg/sec.
tools.maturity: pgmq: young. SKIP LOCKED pattern: production-grade (used by many applications).
tools.license: PostgreSQL License (permissive) for pgmq. SKIP LOCKED is native Postgres.
tools.python_macos_compat: pgmq requires extension installation. SKIP LOCKED is native — no extension needed.
tools.transitive_dependency_risk: Low for SKIP LOCKED (native). Medium for pgmq (extension dependency).
tools.operational_complexity: Medium — queue management adds operational burden. Risk of turning Postgres into orchestration tar pit — Postgres should not become a job scheduler.
tools.duplicates_existing: No — no durable queue in Rig Relay currently.
tools.risks_undermining_artifact_first: Medium — queue items must not become canonical event truth. Coordination events.jsonl remains canonical. Queue items are ephemeral runtime state.
tools.risks_undermining_postgres_authority: Medium — risk of overloading Postgres with queue management. Postgres is the operational substrate, not a message broker.
tools.helps_other_domains: Low — current coordination store (file-backed) and future Postgres advisory locks cover coordination needs without queue semantics.
tools.recommendation: park — SKIP LOCKED pattern on coordination_lease table may be useful for lease cleanup and stale lease reclamation. Full queue semantics (pgmq) is overkill. Do not turn Postgres into orchestration tar pit.

tools.name: Zstandard (expanded usage)
tools.what_it_is: Fast compression algorithm with excellent ratio. Already a canonical dependency (zstandard>=0.25.0) but only used for teleport diff compression.
tools.what_it_is_not: A replacement for gzip in all cases. Not encryption. Not a redaction mechanism.
tools.maturity: Production-grade. RFC 8878. Facebook/Meta maintained. Python bindings via zstandard package (stable since 0.15).
tools.python_macos_compat: Already a dependency. Pre-built wheels. No additional cost.
tools.transitive_dependency_risk: Zero — already a canonical dependency. Expanding usage does not add new dependencies.
tools.operational_complexity: Low — already integrated. Expanding to session bundles, archive compaction, and export packages is natural.
tools.duplicates_existing: gzip for session lifecycle compaction. Zstandard provides better ratio and speed. gzip should remain as fallback.
tools.risks_undermining_artifact_first: None — compression is storage optimization. Artifacts remain JSON/JSONL/CSV. Compression must not obscure content-light inspection.
tools.risks_undermining_postgres_authority: None — compression for cold storage and export bundles.
tools.helps_cockpit_ux: No — compression is for storage, not UX.
tools.helps_procurement: Yes — zstd-compressed evidence bundles and export packages for procurement packs.
tools.helps_telemetry_evidence: Yes — zstd-compressed cold evidence archives. Zstd-compressed debug/support packets.
tools.recommendation: promote — Phase 1. Expand Zstandard usage: session bundle compression, archive compaction, export package compression, cold evidence archives. Zero dependency risk (already canonical). High compression ratio upside over gzip (20-40% smaller, 3-5x faster).

tools.name: orjson
tools.what_it_is: Fast, correct JSON library for Python. Rust-backed. 3-5x faster than stdlib json for loads/dumps. Supports dataclasses, datetime, UUID natively.
tools.what_it_is_not: A schema validator. Not a replacement for jsonschema or Pydantic. Not a content-light enforcement mechanism.
tools.maturity: Production-grade. 3.10.x stable. Used by FastAPI, many ASGI frameworks.
tools.python_macos_compat: Pre-built wheels for macOS arm64 and x86_64. ~5MB wheel.
tools.transitive_dependency_risk: Low — orjson has few dependencies. Stable API.
tools.operational_complexity: Low — drop-in replacement for stdlib json in most cases.
tools.duplicates_existing: Yes — stdlib json covers all current JSON needs. orjson is faster but the current JSON workload does not justify the speedup.
tools.risks_undermining_artifact_first: Medium — if orjson bypasses Pydantic/jsonschema validation in a fast path, schema governance is compromised. Must never be a validation bypass.
tools.helps_cockpit_ux: Low — cockpit projection payloads are small. JSON parsing is not the bottleneck.
tools.helps_telemetry_evidence: Low — JSONL line-by-line parsing is not the bottleneck.
tools.recommendation: park — evaluate only if a measured JSON bottleneck is identified in Phase 1 measurement harness. Current JSON workload (SSE chunks, small JSONL lines, single-file reads) does not justify the dependency. If adopted, must enforce that orjson fast path cannot bypass jsonschema/Pydantic validation.

tools.name: msgspec
tools.what_it_is: Fast serialization/validation library. MessagePack and JSON support. Struct type for schema-first deserialization. Rust-backed.
tools.what_it_is_not: A Pydantic replacement. Not a full schema validation framework. MessagePack support is not needed in Rig Relay.
tools.operational_complexity: Medium — msgspec Struct types would duplicate Pydantic models. Two model systems to maintain.
tools.duplicates_existing: Yes — Pydantic v2 already provides fast model validation and serialization via pydantic-core (Rust-backed). msgspec would duplicate the model layer.
tools.risks_undermining_artifact_first: Medium — two model systems risk inconsistency. Pydantic is the canonical model layer.
tools.recommendation: reject — Pydantic v2 + pydantic-core already provides Rust-backed fast serialization. Adding msgspec duplicates the model layer without clear benefit. Pydantic should be exploited harder before evaluating alternative serialization.

tools.name: Pydantic v2 / pydantic-core (exploited harder)
tools.what_it_is: Already the canonical model layer. pydantic-core is Rust-backed for fast validation/serialization. model_dump_json() is the standard serialization path.
tools.what_it_is_not: Currently underused — many modules use stdlib json.loads/dumps where Pydantic model_validate/model_dump_json would provide type safety and validation.
tools.operational_complexity: Low — already familiar. Expanding usage reduces operational complexity by unifying on a single model layer.
tools.duplicates_existing: Partially — many modules use stdlib json instead of Pydantic. Not duplication, but missed opportunity for type safety.
remediation_gaps: ReceiptStore manifest lines use raw json.dumps instead of Pydantic model serialization
EventStore append uses raw json.dumps instead of EventEnvelope model serialization
CoordinationStore event payloads use _canonical_json.dump_canonical_json() instead of Pydantic model_dump(mode='json')
ReportStore uses raw json.dumps for report lines — Report model should be Pydantic
ContextCompiler receipt uses hashlib over raw text — should use Pydantic model serialization for deterministic hashing
tools.recommendation: promote — Phase 2 (Port Definition). Expand Pydantic usage: replace stdlib json.loads/dumps at module boundaries with Pydantic model_validate/model_dump_json. This provides free type safety, schema validation, and faster serialization (pydantic-core is Rust-backed) without adding a new dependency.

tools.name: SQLGlot
tools.what_it_is: SQL parser, transpiler, and optimizer. Can parse DuckDB SQL, transpile to Postgres SQL, and detect dialect-specific features.
tools.what_it_is_not: A query engine. Not a database driver. Not a replacement for writing correct SQL.
tools.python_macos_compat: Pure Python. No system dependencies. Small package.
tools.operational_complexity: Low — used as a linting/validation tool, not a runtime dependency.
tools.duplicates_existing: No — no SQL parsing/transpilation in the codebase currently.
tools.risks_undermining_artifact_first: None — SQL tooling, not data storage.
tools.risks_undermining_postgres_authority: None — helps write correct Postgres SQL.
tools.recommendation: park — Phase 7. Useful for: (1) detecting DuckDB-specific SQL in portable projections, (2) validating that Postgres migration SQL is dialect-correct, (3) linting against forbidden SQL patterns. But not needed until DuckDB↔Postgres projection parity is tested (Phase 4). Do not auto-transpile without equivalence tests.

tools.name: Iceberg / Delta-style lakehouse table formats
tools.what_it_is: Apache Iceberg and Delta Lake are large-scale table formats for data lakes. Provide ACID transactions, time travel, and schema evolution over object storage (S3, GCS).
tools.what_it_is_not: A local analytics format. Not appropriate for Rig Relay's local-first architecture. Not a replacement for Parquet or Postgres.
tools.maturity: Production-grade at petabyte scale. Used by Netflix, Apple, Adobe.
tools.python_macos_compat: PyIceberg and delta-rs exist but are heavyweight. Require JVM (Iceberg) or Rust (delta-rs) plus object storage infrastructure.
tools.transitive_dependency_risk: Very high — iceberg/delta dependencies include JVM, Hadoop, object storage SDKs.
tools.operational_complexity: Very high — designed for clusters, not local operation.
tools.duplicates_existing: Completely different scale category than Rig Relay's needs.
tools.recommendation: reject — local-first architecture does not justify lakehouse table formats. Parquet snapshots (already in use) provide sufficient derived analytical storage. If future hosted telemetry warehouse needs arise, evaluate Iceberg/Delta at that time.

tools.name: LanceDB / separate vector stores
tools.what_it_is: LanceDB is an embedded vector database using Lance columnar format. Provides vector similarity search without a separate server.
tools.what_it_is_not: A Postgres extension. Not integrated with the operational substrate.
tools.maturity: Young — LanceDB is newer than pgvector. Lance format is promising but less battle-tested.
tools.transitive_dependency_risk: Medium — LanceDB adds its own storage engine, query engine, and format.
tools.operational_complexity: Medium — separate vector database alongside Postgres. Fragments operational authority.
tools.duplicates_existing: No existing vector database. But pgvector inside Postgres would avoid fragmentation.
tools.risks_undermining_postgres_authority: High — separate vector database fragments the operational substrate. Postgres should be the unified operational store.
tools.recommendation: reject — for contrast case only. pgvector (Postgres extension) is preferred because it keeps vector search inside the canonical operational substrate. Do not fragment operational authority with a separate database unless Postgres-based vector search proves insufficient.
